name: Hyperbeam

modes.label: HD participant-hour
modes.note: 60×$0.007 per participant-minute; not per VM-hour. Graduated monthly volume discounts unmodeled. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: 10,000 free participant-minutes/month = $70 base-rate equivalent. Shared allowance; never subtract again as free.monthly_credit.

features.ip_note: Sessions run in NA/EU/AS regions on mixed server providers with no fixed IP range; bring your own HTTP proxy via PAC file (WebRTC not proxied); no managed proxies.
features.browser_profile_retention: Profiles not accessed for three months expire and are automatically deleted.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.

Calculator counts all participants, not just participants after the first. One browser watched by three people can incur three participant streams. Headless use with zero watchers has no verified tariff.
Embedded save states, multi-user control and WebGL are documented; no separate storage/proxy/CAPTCHA tariff found. Machine resource guarantees are unpublished.
Graduated monthly volume discounts apply automatically: 5% from 60k participant-minutes, 10% from 300k, 15% from 600k, 25% from 3M, 35% from 6M, 45% from 12M. Not modelled.

fleet.verification: Introductory monthly usage explicitly no card.
fleet.notes: Participant-minute credits and shared-session participant counts are not concurrent VM quotas. No exact new-account session fleet cap/raise process located.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The Hyperbeam profile API allows you to persist session state including bookmarks, history, passwords, and cookies which can be loaded into another session at a later time.
snapshot_auto.note: Closest thing: with profile=true (or profile=<session_id>) the Chrome profile is saved 'when the new session is terminated' and must be passed explicitly to load it. Browser-profile data only (cookies, history, passwords, bookmarks, tabs), opt-in per request; no machine/memory state. Profiles unused for three months are deleted.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: `save` = `true` creates a new persisted profile you can load from. If a session ID is provided, then the profile associated with the session ID will be overwritten.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint; profile save happens at session termination only (profile.load / profile.save let you fork a profile into a new one). No memory state.

harness_api.quote: Dispatch Endpoints: Initiate a virtual machine instance ... Starting a Chromium Session ... Starting a Android Emulator ... Starting a Console Emulator
harness_api.note: Embeddable multiplayer cloud browser/emulator streamed to end users; APIs cover sessions, roles, permissions, tabs and input events. No agent harness, no command exec.

ingress_rules.quote: When using token authentication, a token is added as a query parameter to the cloud computer’s embed URL. This ensures only users that were provided the embed URL have access to the cloud computer—malicious actors cannot gain access via the session ID
ingress_rules.note: Default token-authenticated embed URL; optional webhook authentication (your endpoint returns {"authorized": true/false} per connecting user); per-user roles/permissions, control_disable_default, remove users via session endpoints. Access is only via the streamed browser; no arbitrary ports.
